pois.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
pois.description: One of Tokyo's largest parks — 58 hectares mixing French formal garden, English landscape garden, and Japanese traditional garden. A national garden (imperial retreat until 1949). The most celebrated hanami spot in Tokyo: 1,100 cherry trees of 65 varieties bloom March to May.

pois.name: Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower
pois.description: At 200m and 50 floors, the Cocoon Tower is one of Tokyo's most distinctive skyscrapers — its interlocking diamond-mesh exoskeleton wraps the building like a cocoon. Home to Mode Gakuen (fashion/design), Tokyo Medical & Dental University, and HAL Tokyo (IT). Completed 2008.

pois.name: Tokyu Kabukicho Tower
pois.description: Tokyo's newest mixed-use megastructure (2023, 192m), towering over Kabukicho — the city's most intense entertainment district. Contains a cinema complex, live music venues, hotels, restaurants, and a rooftop observation deck. The anchoring landmark of the new Kabukicho Square redevelopment.

pois.name: Shinjuku Nomura Building
pois.description: The tallest building in Shinjuku at 220m (1978). One of the original 'Skyscraper District' towers — the first cluster of high-rises west of Shinjuku Station that transformed Tokyo's skyline. The observation deck on the 50th floor offers panoramic views over the city.

pois.name: Hanazono Shrine
pois.description: A quiet Shinto shrine tucked between the glass towers and the neon of Kabukicho. Founded in the Edo period, it's considered the guardian shrine of Shinjuku. The night-lit vermillion torii gates, just steps from the entertainment district, are a famous contrast of sacred and profane Tokyo.
